transcript:
Header: 2026-08-12 16:00 UTC | Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Sam Patel (Redwood AE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendez (Andes Ventures - Head Partnerships), Priya Sharma (Andes - Sales Ops), Evelyn Park (Andes - VP Partnerships)

Summary (auto): Quick pipeline sync to review co-sell opportunities and next steps.

[00:00] Sam Patel: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we got about 45 minutes, want to run through the pipeline you sent and talk next steps, is that right carlos?
[00:12] Carlos Mendez: yeah thanks sam, appreciate it, we have like 7 active opps where we think redwood can be the inference partner, a couple are in procurement but three look promising for pilot in q3
[00:26] Lena Ortiz: awesome, quick question - for the pilots are you expecting hosted api or private deployment? just to plan eng bandwidth and sla expectations
[00:36] Carlos Mendez: good point, evelyn and i talked, the preference is hosted for fast time to value but two logos require VPC or private due to data residency, so mixed motion
[00:48] Evelyn Park: yep, the finance platform customer will need a VPC and SOC2 evidence; the adtech one is ok with hosted + contractual DPA
[00:59] Sam Patel: ok makes sense. we can support mixed approach — we have hosted for quick onboarding and private/dedicated for customers with residency or compliance needs. we should map each opp to recommended deployment and expected time to value
[01:15] Priya Sharma: can you also clarify pricing differences and reserved capacity commit requirements? some of our partners want predictable cost models
[01:25] Sam Patel: absolutely — i'll include a pricing snapshot in the deck, and note dedicated/reserved commit models; also offer burst capacity for short term spikes so it doesn't block deal progress
[01:37] Carlos Mendez: on co-sell mechanics, how do you handle lead registration and commission or referral fees? we need a simple playbook for our reps
[01:46] Sam Patel: good question — typical model is joint registration sheet + lead owner column, we track via partner portal. commission terms are negotiable per contract but we can propose standard slate in the co-sell guidelines i send
[01:58] Evelyn Park: and what about enablement — how much enablement material do you provide? we need slide decks, battlecards, and maybe 1:1 training for our AE team
[02:07] Lena Ortiz: we have a co-sell kit — slides, technical playbooks, common objections, and an SE-hosted workshop. we can schedule a 90-minute enablement and record it for your team
[02:19] Carlos Mendez: great. for the three pilots, can you run a perf baseline? our customers care about latency and cost per token
[02:29] Lena Ortiz: yes we can instrument a benchmark. do you have sample prompts or workloads? ideally we test representative sequences and concurrency patterns
[02:38] Priya Sharma: i can attach a sample workload spreadsheet after the call
[02:44] Sam Patel: perfect. we'll need expected p95 latency targets per customer and success criteria — eg 95th pctl < 250ms for interactive, or cost per 1000 tokens below X for batch use
[02:58] Carlos Mendez: sounds good. one of the competitors we've seen is anthropic for safety-focused customers and we also get asked about openai for ease of use
[03:08] Sam Patel: yea we hear that a lot — we'll give you messaging to differentiate on cost and private deployment options; redwood's value is predictable unit economics and multi-deployment flexibility
[03:18] Lena Ortiz: also we can show a comparison matrix vs anthropic and openai on private deploy, latency, and batching capability, and we'll surface our quantization/throughput advantages for batch workloads
[03:31] Evelyn Park: compliance side — the finance customer requires SOC2 type 2 and KMS key control, what is required from our legal to push forward?
[03:41] Sam Patel: we can share SOC2 report and our security whitepaper, and for KMS we support customer-managed keys on Private deployments; i'll attach the docs and legal can review
[03:52] Priya Sharma: perfect. also question on branding — do you allow co-branded collateral for joint pitches?
[03:59] Sam Patel: yes co-branded decks are fine, we usually have a simple co-marketing agreement and joint logos for case studies if both parties agree
[04:11] Carlos Mendez: ok logistically, what's the pilot timeline you recommend? we want 6 week pilots for the adtech and finance ones
[04:20] Lena Ortiz: 6 weeks is reasonable: week 1 onboarding and data prep, weeks 2-4 benchmarks and tuning, week 5 validation with customer, week 6 handoff and results + next steps
[04:31] Sam Patel: we'll propose that timeline in the pilot plan. action items: i send deck and pipeline template, lena builds bench plan, carlos shares logos and contacts
[04:42] Priya Sharma: we'll also assign a partner owner internally and share a contact sheet
[04:47] Sam Patel: any blockers we should know about?
[04:50] Carlos Mendez: only the finance customer procurement window — they close out vendor approvals mid-september, so we need pilot started before end of august ideally
[04:59] Sam Patel: noted — we'll prioritize that one for early pilot and allocate SRE/SE time accordingly
[05:05] Evelyn Park: final, can you put together short risk matrix? procurement, security, and pricing risk per opp
[05:12] Lena Ortiz: yes we can include a 1-pager risk matrix in the packet
[05:17] Sam Patel: awesome, thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the deck and pipeline spreadsheet by friday. next meeting after you review the materials, likely w/c 2026-08-24 for exec intro
[05:29] Carlos Mendez: thanks all, appreciate it
[05:32] Priya Sharma: thanks, bye
[05:34] (call ends)
